body.cap: At CES 2024, mpWAV received CES Innovation Awards in the ‘Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps’ and ‘Digital Health’ categories for its hearing assistance application ‘ClearSense Audio.’ | Photo by AVING News

body.x: mpWAV, led by CEO Park Hyeong-min, showcased its hearing assistance application, ‘ClearSense Audio,’ at CES 2024, held in Las Vegas from January 9 to 12. With this application, the company received the CES 2024 Innovation Awards Honoree in the ‘Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps’ and ‘Digital Health’ categories.

mpWAV actively introduced its award-winning hearing assistance application, ‘ClearSense Audio.’ ClearSense Audio goes beyond simply replacing the basic hearing aid function to alleviate hearing loss issues in older people. It helps everyone, including those without hearing impairment, hear desired sounds clearly in noisy environments.

mpWAV, founded to productize core technologies for advanced voice enhancement and voice recognition, boasts a rich research experience in the field. Professor Park Hyeong-min and his research team from Sogang University successfully developed essential technologies for voice enhancement and recognition applicable in real-world complex noise environments. The technologies include multi-channel acoustic echo cancellation, beamforming, signal separation, and robust speech recognition. The company offers comprehensive solutions encompassing hardware and software for various voice interface applications, ranging from innovative hearing aids to smart homes, smart cars, electronics, robots, kiosks, and voice chatting in diverse meeting systems.

A mpWAV representative stated, “Many challenges arise for the middle-aged and elderly due to hearing loss and various surrounding noises, hindering effective communication with others. We noticed that a significant portion of this demographic, not necessarily suffering from severe hearing loss, faces discomfort. Moreover, even those who need hearing aids are reluctant due to the exposure of wearing them, excessive auditory stimulation from sound amplification, and high costs.”

To address these issues, mpWAV developed its technology, allowing users to use their smartphones and earphones to selectively remove distortion-free noise in noisy acoustic environments, enabling them to hear desired sounds anytime. This approach not only resolves fundamental issues with hearing aids but also presents an affordable app format, allowing the general public to access hearing assistance when needed easily.
In this way, mpWAV has succeeded at CES 2024 by receiving innovation awards in two categories, recognizing its contribution to improving users’ quality of life and realizing social value.

body.x: An official stated, “Our solution is not influenced by language characteristics, allowing us to quickly enter foreign markets without significant barriers. We anticipate an official launch in the early months of this year, leveraging CES 2024 to enhance visibility. After the release, we plan to continuously evolve our app based on user feedback, satisfying ongoing needs. Additionally, discussions are underway for collaborations with partners requiring hardware and software technology related to voice interfaces, aiming to introduce various application products.”

Furthermore, they added, “During this exhibition period, we observed significant interest from U.S. and European companies in our technology. Meaningful discussions were also held with venture-accelerating companies located in Silicon Valley.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
